### A write set, a first effect contract: prove --writes refutes the setter that writes a protected field and proves its honest twin

change `qrqtplwqnrml` · [log `e461fc676833`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/f8bc7b54-f877-4ee9-8e3a-b5ffbba621bc/e461fc6768339d631679cf98e291738c3b8059215d201c1c2646b2aab42d83a7.jsonl.gz)

The state stream's steps 4 and 5, the checking side. prove --writes this.displayName (own checker only) states which fields of a method's receiver and object parameters it may write. The check proves the frame with the property: after a normal return every other field of those inputs is unchanged, a primitive by value and a String or object by identity through the new p == \old(p) term. The frame is conjoined to the assertion, so a write outside the set is refuted by the harness and its witness runs on a JVM. Inside the call the engine refuses, by name, a write to anything else that existed before it: a static field, an array, an object no input is (even one a named field holds), or a class initialization, whose objects would look new to the call. This generalizes Engine::keeps through bmc::Options::frame. The cache refuses such a check, since its key does not read the write set.

### A library method the own checker can't run may be replaced by a stand-in sampled against it on a JVM (prove --stand-in), and a result that used one says it rests on it

change `qlylowvomrqr` · [log `e461fc676833`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/f8bc7b54-f877-4ee9-8e3a-b5ffbba621bc/e461fc6768339d631679cf98e291738c3b8059215d201c1c2646b2aab42d83a7.jsonl.gz)

Step 3, option 2, of the state stream's brief. Spring's bean wrapper resolves a property through its introspection caches and java.beans and calls the setter with Method.invoke, on every path of DataBinder.bind (example 286). Observing those caches is refused, and running them would need models of java.beans and java.lang.reflect. So the binding path gets a stand-in instead. Each public static method of the stand-in class (but main) replaces an instance method: its first parameter's class is the exact class of the receivers it covers, the rest of its descriptor is the method's. A call resolving to that method on a receiver of exactly that class runs the stand-in. A subclass's receiver, and the stand-in's own calls, run the method as written, so a stand-in hands back what it does not cover. Its main prints one line per sample with the method's outcome and the stand-in's. The tool runs it first on the check's class path and takes the stand-in only if every sample is the same, refusing it by the first input that differs, or when nothing is sampled, or for a public method that replaces nothing. A result that used a stand-in names it among what it rests on, with the number of samples, as sampled evidence and not a proof. A refutation through one is still replayed on a JVM. JBMC and --cache are refused.

Verified by lib/tests/stand_in.rs on the fixture lib/tests/fixtures/stand-ins, a reflective property writer. With the stand-in, a claim the method leaves undecided is proved and the stand-in is named; a refutation replays on a JVM. A subclass receiver, and a bean the stand-in hands back, stop at the method's gap as before. A stand-in that forgets 'Age', one that samples nothing, and one with a public helper are refused. Switching off the exact-receiver check, or the sample comparison, by mutation makes a test fail. test_costs run --changed passes, after the proof cache's projection named the new option. 286's own stand-in is drafted, not committed: sampled against 5.3.19's setPropertyValue, its 38,400 samples all match. ### A preservation proof is non-vacuous only with a witness outside the allowed change, and accept.py asks the outcome to say so

change `ymzlyksqouqq` · [log `e461fc676833`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/f8bc7b54-f877-4ee9-8e3a-b5ffbba621bc/e461fc6768339d631679cf98e291738c3b8059215d201c1c2646b2aab42d83a7.jsonl.gz)

Step 4 of the evidence stream's brief. A regression check made as a property of the pair of versions (lib/src/pairing.rs, the route of examples 289's and 290's preservation) proves RegressionPair.agree, which returns true on an input inside the allowed change without calling either version. The property check's vacuity probe asked only for an input of the assumption, so it called a proof non-vacuous even when every assumed input lay inside the change. The control: example 289's preservation through its own driver, with only --unchanged-unless replaced by true, was verified and non-vacuous (a capped 5 s probe). 290's recorded witness, servlets=[], lies inside its own allowed change.

The fix: a verified pair with an allowed change is checked once more, meantToChange against result over the same assumption, domain and class path. A proof makes the statement vacuous; a witness, replayed as any is, becomes the statement's, with the new stated.vacuity.outside naming the change. The regression harness's own probe sets outside too, since that harness returns before the probe on an input in the scope. Now the true control is vacuous, 289 with its own change is non-vacuous at servletPath="" (0.3 s more) and 290 at servlets=[0] (capped probes, recorded in both examples' notes). accept.py refuses an establishment of a task with an allowed change whose outcome does not say its witness lies outside that change (unbound) or names another (fail). So 289's and 290's accepted preservation answers are refused until a rerun on a checker with this fix; the other six stay accepted.

Verified: lib/tests/pairing.rs a_pairs_proof_is_vacuous_when_the_allowed_change_covers_every_assumed_input (tool tier, fails without the fix with NonVacuous), three new cases in examples/tools/test_accept.py, the 289 checkout test now expecting preservation refused for this reason; test_costs.py run --changed 8 of 8, estimate, tag and lint clean; validate_example.py 289 and 290 pass. lib/README.md describes the check.

### An observed initializer is refused where it wrote into a value another class holds or changed the JDK's settings: every value of a class it initialized besides is compared in full

change `vqquvmnmmoqx` · [log `e461fc676833`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/f8bc7b54-f877-4ee9-8e3a-b5ffbba621bc/e461fc6768339d631679cf98e291738c3b8059215d201c1c2646b2aab42d83a7.jsonl.gz)

The challenge stream's binding countermodels (klqnuoxw, inbox item I011) showed three proofs a JVM contradicts. The observation compared a class the initialization initialized besides only as far as it held its fields, so a write into an object another class holds (bc.Boxed) and a lambda of Hooks put in place of another of Hooks' (bc.Rehooked) went unseen. It also read the default locale before the initialization, so an initializer that set it (bc.Relocaled) was observed as if it had not. Their fixtures and JVM test were copied from klqnuoxw unchanged.

The observer (lib/src/observed/ObservedInitializer.java, Describe) now describes in full each value it does not hold, in each class initialized besides the observed one and in that class initialized alone. An object of the application is described by every field its classes declare. A lambda is described by the method it calls, read from its class's constant pool (the observer's JVM gets --add-exports for that), and by the values it captured. A JDK collection is described by its elements, sorted where the class keeps no order, and a float by its bits. observe (lib/src/observed.rs) compares these descriptions and refuses a value with none, with why. The observer also reads the default locale, the time zone and the system properties again after the initialization, and a change is refused with the setting. The format gains on.changed, plus d or why beside u; Slot, Object and the identity are unchanged.

examples/307-*/records/step-6-call-level.md is the note and step-6-call-level-probes.json the runs. lib/tests/fixtures/callee-countermodels/prototype-one-function.patch (against kskmpmny, git 10b5d9c0, after prototype-model.patch) names a callee's outcome by the key of the state at its entry, as a loop's state past the bound is named, and checks no side condition. With it, at the claim's frozen parameters and assumption, in capped probes (4 GB, 300 s): with the relation at crypt_raw on JDK 25, preservation is verified in 79 s (878 MB) and the mutant is a violation in 58 s, replayed on a JVM; with it at hashpw(byte[], String), preservation is verified in 53 s on JDK 21 and the run is killed at 4 GB on JDK 25, and the mutant has no verdict under the claim's seven salts (the first candidate has salt = null) and is a violation under one valid salt. The JDK 25 difference: hashpw(byte[], String) calls Integer.parseInt, whose bytecode the checker follows, and JDK 25's parseInt(String, int) calls String.format(String, Object[]), which shared::reach takes as a way back into the application since kskmpmny. The fixture gains the row parsed (Parsing.java, a callee that calls Integer.parseInt): verified on JDK 21 and no verdict on JDK 25 on kskmpmny, in under a second.

The prototype against the fixture's rows: by formula it falsely proves wiped and counted (what the callee writes is not in its outcome); with a relation by content added it falsely proves table, seeded, helped and aliased too. No other row turns. So the rows separate a rule with its side conditions from one without.

**What was found.** I wrote five pairs of small methods in `lib/tests/fixtures/pairing-countermodels`. Each pair gives different results when each version runs alone on a JVM, yet the checker proves the two versions agree:
- **Shared JDK state (`locale`):** the previous version sets a Turkish default locale, and the new version then lowercases under it.
- **Shared library static (`flag`):** without `--before-classpath`, both versions read and write one copy of a library field, so the new version reads what the previous one wrote.
- **Exceptions by category (`thrown`, `argument`):** two unrelated `RuntimeException`s count as the same, and so do `IllegalArgumentException` and a subclass of it.
- **The allowed change (`scoped`):** the `--unchanged-unless` expression runs new-version code before both calls. One that is false everywhere but sets the default locale makes the two versions agree.

**Call order matters.** With the versions' roles swapped, the shared-static case comes back as a violation, and it does in either order with `--before-classpath`. The swapped locale case comes back "unverifiable" only because the interpreter lowercases without looking at the locale. The checker's answer there is cautious, not wrong.

7. **Bounds:** a task's own bound can lower the claim's, so a proof at a smaller bound is accepted for the claim's.

**Reply:**

Cycle 4 is committed as `zmpzxkqn`. Preservation's fix for my earlier reach countermodels (`qopxypnn`) holds, but I found five false proofs past it.

**The hole:** when the checker decides two versions run the same code, it compares each method's code but never a class's superclass or interfaces. It also doesn't check that both versions reach the same methods, only that each method one version reaches exists, unchanged, in the other.

**The cases:** the new fixture `lib/tests/fixtures/supertype-countermodels` has two versions in which every method is the same text and only three class headers differ. On a JVM each pair of versions returns 2 against 1, or the new one throws.
- **`rebased`:** the same static call resolves through a different superclass in each version.
- **`marked`:** an `instanceof` of an interface only the previous version's class implements.
- **`cast`:** a cast to that interface, which throws `ClassCastException` in the new version.
